\textbf{Source.} Tadelis (2013), \emph{Game Theory: An Introduction}, Exercise 5.1, p.~95 {[}PDF p.~114{]}. Answer in the source: none (the preface, p.~xiii, says about half of the exercises are solved on Princeton UP's website). Reproduced verbatim.

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Prove Proposition 5.1.}
\end{quote}

\textbf{Referred to in the statement.} Proposition 5.1 (Tadelis pp.~80--81 {[}PDF p.~99--100{]}) (reproduced from the book):

\begin{quote}
\textbf{Proposition 5.1} Consider a strategy profile \(s = (s_1, s_2, \ldots, s_n)\). If \(s\) is either

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  a strict dominant strategy equilibrium,
\item
  the unique survivor of IESDS, or
\item
  the unique rationalizable strategy profile,
\end{enumerate}

then \(s\) is the unique Nash equilibrium.
\end{quote}
